detail.longDescription: Some LLM API models charge a higher per-token rate once a prompt passes a length threshold. I am writing a cost estimator in JavaScript and I am not sure how to model this correctly. First, is the higher rate applied to the whole request once the threshold is crossed, or only to the tokens above the threshold (like tax brackets)? Second, is the threshold compared against total input tokens, or only against the non-cached input tokens? Third, does the higher rate also apply to output tokens and cached-input tokens? What is a correct way to calculate the cost of a request that sits just above or just below the threshold?
